set.descent_text: From the summit, reverse the upper route: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, then work left to a single rappel of about 120 ft, near the southern edge of the Catwalk, that drops straight onto the Upper Saddle; otherwise downclimb the whole route. A single 60 m rope can manage the rappel from the slung horn if you trend right as you go, and a shorter 70 ft rappel sits beside it. Finding the way is the main difficulty, because the whole face shows signs of traffic and the line is not obvious from above. From the Upper Saddle do not drop into the first gully heading southeast; go farther west to the climbers' trails that lead to the Lower Saddle, then follow Garnet Canyon back to the trailhead.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle, pass left of the smooth pinnacle called the Needle and climb the gully close beside it (the tunnel known as the Eye of the Needle is optional); the scramble of roughly 1,400 ft to the Upper Saddle at about 13,160 ft is a serious undertaking in its own right. From the saddle, hike and scramble about 70 m north-northeast to the usual rope-up spot beneath the Wittich Crack, just before the Belly Roll.

review.notes: Descent facts from the route page and the rappel area description; approach from the route page and the Garnet Canyon timings page.

set.descent_text: Descend the upper Owen-Spalding route: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, then rappel about 120 ft onto the Upper Saddle. A single 60 m rope can do it from the slung horn if you angle to the right, though two ropes or a 70 m are more usual, and a shorter 70 ft rappel sits beside it; confident parties downclimb the 5.4 ground instead and skip the midsummer lines. The way down is hard to find, so note landmarks on the way up. From the Upper Saddle do not drop into the first gully heading southeast (the couloir below the saddle toward Wall Street cliffs out); work farther west to the climbers' trails that lead down to the Lower Saddle, then follow Garnet Canyon out to the Lupine Meadows trailhead.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle follow the Owen-Spalding line left of the Needle pinnacle and up the gully close beside it, then diverge right and cross a wide, gentle couloir to reach Wall Street, a huge ledge at about 12,800 ft. Note that couloir for the descent, since it drops from the Upper Saddle and cliffs out. Wall Street is easy walking until it narrows and becomes exposed at its end, where parties rope up to start the Golden Stair pitch.

review.notes: Both from the Upper Exum route page, descent cross-checked on the Owen-Spalding page and the rappel description.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the Wall Street ledge. Most parties continue up the Upper Exum Ridge to the summit and descend the standard way (downclimb Sargent's Chimney and rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle). Parties not continuing can reverse the Wall Street approach, taking care at the narrow, exposed step at its end, and descend to the Lower Saddle that way.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle go north toward the peak, but rather than gaining the ridge, contour down the saddle's east side and scramble east until you meet a black band of rock running east-west. Follow the foot of the band over a small saddle whose two halves are different colours, drop slightly, and a short way past the low point of the band look for a fourth-class ramp that goes back left (south). The ramp climbs a few hundred feet to the foot of pitch one, a big chimney or the better-liked face just to its right.

review.notes: Approach from the route page; the end at Wall Street and the descent choices from the route page and the Gold Face and Wooden Ships pages.

set.descent_text: The route ends at Wall Street. From there either continue up the Upper Exum Ridge to the summit and descend the standard way, or reverse the Wall Street approach (with its exposed step at the narrow end) back toward the Lower Saddle. The standard descent from the summit downclimbs Sargent's Chimney, rappels about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then heads west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails to the Lower Saddle.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Take the Lower Exum approach from the Lower Saddle to the black dike trail, then traverse in along a higher ledge and scramble nearly up to the Lower Exum crest, stopping where the ground needs a rope. Above and to the right a short bulge gives onto a corner that faces right; that is where the climbing starts. Parties may also climb the first two pitches of the Lower Exum and step down east to reach the line.

review.notes: Route page gives start, end at Wall Street and two descent options.

set.descent_text: The climb finishes on a small subsidiary summit. Getting off it takes a drop of about 30 ft, rappelled from a threaded anchor or downclimbed, gets you off it. From there most parties angle up along a ledge until they meet the Exum Ridge where the Wind Tunnel begins, and finish by the Upper Exum; with good snow the Ford Couloir is another way up. From the summit, use the standard Owen-Spalding descent: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle follow the faint Black Dike trail east across the base of the Lower Exum Ridge to the Petzoldt Ridge, the next ridge to the right of the Exum. The climb begins a little right of the crest. An ice axe may be needed in early to mid season.

review.notes: Route page gives the minor summit, thread and the two ways onward; approach from the route and the Beyer East Face page.

set.descent_text: At the top of the buttress, make a short rappel into a notch, where a broad ramp angling left (west) joins the Exum Ridge above the Golden Stair. Continue up the Upper Exum to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle follow the faint Black Dike trail east beneath the Lower Exum Ridge to the foot of the Petzoldt buttress. The original start up the Stettner Couloir is no longer favoured because of rockfall; instead start at the base of the buttress, climb up and traverse right for two short pitches to the foot of a left-facing corner.

review.notes: Route page gives the rappel, ramp and variation start.

set.descent_text: Once on top of the ridge, follow a good ledge system north, stow the rope and scramble the last 700 ft or so to the summit; snow higher up may call for detours. Budget roughly two to three hours between Glencoe Col and the ridge top, plus an hour or more of scrambling. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: The usual plan is to camp at the Lower Saddle and take the Black Dike traverse east to Glencoe Col; that crosses Stettner Col, which can be badly hit by rockfall, particularly late in the year. The alternative is to camp at the foot of the Teepe Glacier and climb up from there, which usually needs an ice axe and sometimes crampons for an early start. Glencoe Col can also be bivied, with snow for water. Climbing starts on the ridge's east flank, up a wide ramp of fourth to easy fifth class that runs 400 ft or more.

review.notes: Route page for both approaches, the top-out and the scramble.

set.descent_text: The last pitch ends on top of the Underhill Ridge at about 12,900 ft. Unrope, cross the snow-covered saddle about 50 ft wide, and zigzag up third- and fourth-class ground, avoiding snowfields, to the summit; there is one brief 5.5 step low down and a short 5.4 chimney high up. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle walk the Owen-Spalding trail for about ten minutes until a faint trail branches right (hard to find in the dark, so scout it or wait for light). It runs beneath the Exum, Petzoldt and Underhill ridges and over the base of the Stettner Couloir to Teepe Col. From the col descend on rubble, trending left, for about 200 ft to a low-angle ridge, then walk up north to a ledge system, past a big left-facing corner, to below a right-facing corner about 150 ft tall. The start is about 20 ft left and 20 ft above that point, at cracks beside a prominent roof; allow about 75 minutes from the Lower Saddle.

review.notes: Approach and top-out both from the route page.

set.descent_text: The final pitch ends on top of the initial Underhill buttress, after which you join the Underhill Ridge or one of its variations and follow it up for roughly 300 m to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.

review.notes: Route page gives the finish onto the Underhill Ridge; no approach written because the page only points to a guidebook.

set.descent_text: Above the chockstone crux the couloir broadens to the narrow saddle between the Underhill Ridge and the summit snowfield. Turn left, climb third-class slabs mixed with snow, and take the best line up the snowfield to the top. To get down, either ski the Ford Couloir with some rappels or descend the Owen-Spalding (Sargent's Chimney, a rappel of about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then west of the first southeast gully to the Lower Saddle). The Ford turns dangerous later in the day, and wet slides run there.
set.approach: Two ways reach the foot of the couloir. From the Lower Saddle follow the Black Dike traverse east to the last couloir before Glencoe Col, the high point of the traverse; or come from the east via the Teepe Glacier, Teepe Col and Glencoe Col, which is the more common approach. The couloir lies between the Petzoldt and Underhill ridges. Its narrow lower section is exposed to avalanches that fall from the Ford Couloir, and rockfall also runs down it.

review.notes: Route page; sources agree on its position between the two ridges.

set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit of the tower itself, not the mountain. Rappel once off the summit anchor with a single rope, then swing right into a small notch onto a ledge; take care with the rope ends if using 60 m. Make an exposed move around a boulder (a sling is there to clip) and follow the ledge to a long, exposed fourth-class downclimb of several hundred feet, with a rap station on the way if you prefer. This ends on a large terrace near the foot of the tower, where a last rappel off two fixed pins returns you to your starting ledge. Walk back to your packs at Glencoe Col.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle follow the faint trail through scree along the foot of the Lower Exum, Petzoldt and Underhill ridges to Glencoe Col; this may cross steep firm snow depending on season and hour. Leave packs, axe and other gear at the col and scramble fourth-class ground to a giant ledge below the tower, a feature at the southeast corner of the Underhill Ridge. Watch for rockfall pouring from the Stettner Couloir near the base.

review.notes: Route page for descent and approach.

set.descent_text: The route finishes at the two-bolt rappel anchor on top of the Crystal Tower. Descent follows the tower's own: rappel from the summit, swing right into a notch onto a ledge, traverse around a boulder, and take the lengthy exposed fourth-class downclimb (or an intermediate rap station) to the terrace near the base, then a final rappel to the starting ledge and a walk back to Glencoe Col.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle follow the faint scree trail along the foot of the Lower Exum, Petzoldt and Underhill ridges to Glencoe Col, mindful of rockfall from the Stettner Couloir. The route starts on the left (southeast) side of the tower's base, where the arete between its south and east faces rises from fourth-class ramps and ledges above the col.

review.notes: Both from the route page; descent shared with the tower since the finish is the tower summit.

set.descent_text: The route joins the Exum Ridge at the middle of the V pitch, about 100 ft below what looks like the highest point from the Lower Saddle. Continue to the summit by the Upper Exum. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. From the Lower Saddle follow the Exum Ridge approach, cutting over the Needle's ridge into the gully that lies directly west of the Exum Ridge. Rather than continuing out to Wall Street, scramble north up that gully about 300 ft until directly below the big dihedral in the face. Next, scramble 40 to 50 ft up and right to the foot of the principal corner, near a conspicuous boulder.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: After the crack pitch the route continues three more pitches to the junction with the south ridge. Finish via the Upper Exum to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. The route sits on the west face of the Grand, and its first short pitch is the opening pitch of the West Face of the Exum Ridge. From the Lower Saddle follow the Exum Ridge approach across the Needle ridge into the gully west of the Exum Ridge and scramble up it to the foot of that opening pitch.

review.notes: Route page ties the start to the West Face of the Exum Ridge.

set.descent_text: The last pitch traverses directly across to rejoin the upper Owen-Spalding or the Exum Ridge. Continue to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Follow the Owen-Spalding approach up to the Upper Saddle. The Owen-Spalding rope-up point is to the left; for this route traverse right (south) along a ledge that steadily narrows after about 100 ft, to where a thin crack in a steep corner begins.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The crack leads up to the Cat Walk on the Owen-Spalding. Continue by that route to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Climb from the Lower Saddle to the Upper Saddle as for the Owen-Spalding. The route starts at the usual Owen-Spalding rope-up spot, about 20 ft south of the Belly Roll, where the obvious double cracks break the wall above the saddle.

review.notes: Route page and Owen-Spalding page for the rope-up point.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on a prominent ledge near the standard rappel. Easy ground leads from there to the summit by the Owen-Spalding or the Exum Ridge. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Climb from the Lower Saddle to the Upper Saddle as for the Owen-Spalding. The route starts from the talus there, on the left of the standard rappel line, between the Wittich Crack and the Pseudo Emerson Chimney.

review.notes: Short route page.

set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Climb from the Lower Saddle to the Upper Saddle as for the Owen-Spalding. This line sits right of the Emerson Chimney and left of the Pownall-Gilkey; start by climbing the first 20 m of the Pownall-Gilkey (slab climbing at 5.5, with a bolt and some pitons) to a talus ledge, where the finger crack in the middle of the wall begins.

review.notes: Approach only: the page does not say where it ends.

set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Climb from the Lower Saddle to the Upper Saddle as for the Owen-Spalding. The chimney is about 12 m right of the normal rappel line, near the slings on the crux block that are often visible from below.

review.notes: Approach only: top-out not stated.

set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Climb from the Lower Saddle to the Upper Saddle as for the Owen-Spalding. The chimney starts at the landing of the normal rappel, just right of its line: a deep, dark chimney with wide stemming below a roof.

review.notes: Approach only: top-out not stated.

set.descent_text: The last pitch ends at the Step Across on Wall Street, at the foot of the Golden Staircase. Either continue up the Upper Exum to the summit and descend the standard way (Sargent's Chimney, a rappel of about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, west of the first southeast gully to the Lower Saddle), or retrace your steps along Wall Street and go down the way you came.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Two options. Use the Upper Exum's Wall Street approach, but drop down the gully of the Wall Street Couloir to reach a large ledge on the skier's left, following it to a memorial cairn near the base. Or take the Lower Exum approach; the route begins on the same huge ledge system about 300 to 400 ft farther along, uphill and left of the Lower Exum's first pitch, just downhill of the chorten.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The second pitch ends at the Wind Tunnel of the south ridge, on the Upper Exum. Continue up the Exum Ridge to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Take the Upper Exum approach to the start of Wall Street. It starts toward the left end of Wall Street: head for the chimney, step across a block at third class, and tie in on its right side by a peg.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The top pitch is a scramble over loose talus with a 5.5 step that meets the Upper Exum. Continue up the Exum Ridge to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Take the Upper Exum approach to the start of Wall Street, at about 12,800 ft. An obvious big chimney lies directly left of Flipping Tokens to Hoboken. Scramble to the ledge at its foot, where the rock is thickly covered in bat guano.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The climbing leads into the Exum Ridge at the top of the Lower Exum, just below the Golden Stair. Continue up the Upper Exum to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Follow the approach for the Burgette Arete: the next prominent ramp system just past the one that leads up and left to the Lower Exum, an easy fourth-class walk into a big bowl below the Beckey Couloir. A big cairn marks the first pitch, just short of the crack system of It's Not a Chimney. The panel lies between Gold Face and the Burgette Arete.

review.notes: Route page.

set.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, reached by Lupine Meadows Road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs roughly 6.5 to 7 miles and about 5,000 ft to the Lower Saddle between the Grand and Middle Teton, passing the Platforms, Meadows and Caves camping zones on the way. The trail vanishes briefly across boulder fields, so take the path of least resistance and look for it again beyond. Take the Lower Exum approach from the Lower Saddle, then continue along the Black Dike to the next prominent ramp system just past the one that leads up and left to the Lower Exum; it leads up fourth-class ground into a big bowl below the Beckey Couloir. The arete is east of the Gold Face and shares this approach with It's Not a Chimney.

review.notes: Approach only; the top-out is not stated.

set.descent_text: The fifth pitch ends at the ridge crest. From there go up and right (south) over about 300 ft of fourth-class ground to the top of the Grandstand. Finish by a North Ridge line to reach the summit, then descend the Owen-Spalding; or drop back into the Gunsight notch and go down Mt. Owen's western ledges to Valhalla.
set.approach: The route climbs a northwest-facing shield on the west side of the Grandstand. One approach is up Valhalla Canyon from Cascade Canyon, starting at the west shore of Jenny Lake; the other is the Valhalla Traverse from the Lower Saddle. Once in the West Gunsight Couloir, climb until you spot the vertical cracks that start pitch one, about 350 ft down the couloir from the Gunsight notch at roughly 11,700 ft; then cross to the dark rock ledge beneath them and gear up there. From Valhalla the main dihedral and roof are visible far below, which helps you find it.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: Descend the standard Owen-Spalding route to the Lower Saddle: one or two rappels with a single 60 m rope, combined with scrambling and some route-finding, bring you down. Sargent's Chimney is the first obstacle, followed by a rappel of about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle; from there avoid the first southeast gully and go west to the climbers' trails to the Lower Saddle, then down Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: Four approaches reach the top of the Grandstand and the foot of the North Ridge. The Valhalla Traverse from the Lower Saddle is the standard and usually quickest. The Teton Glacier option (axe and crampons) adds glacier travel and route-finding; Mt. Owen via the Gunsight Notch involves tricky route-finding, unusual rappels and a 5.7 chimney; and the longest route goes up Cascade Canyon, crosses Cascade Creek into Valhalla Canyon and scrambles the west face of the Grandstand. Bivy spots include the Lower Saddle, the moraine below the Teton Glacier and near the top of the Grandstand.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The route finishes on third-class ground about 100 m below the summit (rope up again if you beeline). Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon. The Lower Saddle is also the camp for the Valhalla Traverse.
set.approach: The route begins at the top of the Grandstand, reached in one of three ways. The Valhalla Traverse from the Lower Saddle is the standard but takes at least three hours of loose, snowy and dirty traversing with tricky route-finding. Up the Grandstand from the Teton Glacier is often subject to heavy rockfall. From Mt. Owen, via Teewinot, Koven or the East Ridge, a fast, error-free party needs at least eight hours to get atop the Grandstand, then crosses the Gunsight with three half-rope rappels or a 5.6 downclimb. The face holds snow and ice into summer, so August is best, and an ice axe is likely needed earlier.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The top section is the same as the North Face Highlight Tour and ends on easy ground near the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: The route starts on the Teton Glacier, which is a real glacier with giant crevasses; climb the right side of it and then back left to the foot of the Grandstand. The bergschrund can be a problem. The route begins on the face left of the Grandstand base, climbing ledges and rubble, then trends up and right for several pitches to the Guano Chimney. Take an axe, and perhaps crampons, depending on conditions.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The route merges with the Owen-Spalding at the Double Chimney and follows it to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: The climb starts at the top of the Grandstand, reached as for the North Face Highlight Tour: the Valhalla Traverse from the Lower Saddle, up the Grandstand from the Teton Glacier, or from Mt. Owen. The Valhalla Traverse is the standard and starts at the Lower Saddle, while the Teton Glacier approach tends to see rockfall.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: The route reaches the East Ridge at snow near the top. Put on crampons, climb the snow to the rock and continue to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: The route is on the north face, approached from a bivy on the Teton Glacier. Go up the snow funnel that lies immediately east of the icefall and step over the bergschrund at its head. Gain a small right-trending ledge and follow it for about five pitches of fourth and easy fifth class, including one mandatory rappel about three-quarters of the way along. Pitch one begins at the far end of that ledge.

review.notes: Single report on the route page.

set.descent_text: The route ends near where the Upper Exum reaches the summit snowfields. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: The start is where the Teton Glacier's terminal moraine butts into the mountain. Follow the normal approach to the Teton Glacier from Amphitheater Lake, then turn left atop the highest point of the moraine and follow its crest until it ends against the mountain; cairns mark the way. Bivy sites can be found on top of the moraine near the start. Begin directly from the end of the moraine up a short, steep section to tree-covered ledges on the eastern slopes. An axe and crampons help.

review.notes: Route page.

set.descent_text: At the top of the West Face the route meets the Owen-Spalding near the Owen Chimney; finish up that route to the summit. Descend the standard way: downclimb Sargent's Chimney, rappel about 120 ft to the Upper Saddle, then go west of the first southeast gully to the climbers' trails down to the Lower Saddle and Garnet Canyon.
set.approach: Work across the Valhalla Traverse from the Lower Saddle to the foot of the Black Ice Couloir. Late in a dry season the traverse is mostly dry, with a single airy stretch of frozen gravel and crumbling rock crossing the loose bowl that lies between the northwest ridge and the neighbouring Enclosure ice gully. At the base of the Emotional Rescue Buttress, a single pitch of 5.6 rock, trending up and left, reaches an alcove where the Black Ice Couloir begins.
